content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The LICENSE rule tests the licence granted *to* us. In this outsourcing agreement there is no MSL→IBM licence at all; IBM instead takes **outright ownership** of all IP in Products by assignment (§13.1), with MSL retaining only a narrow right to use assigned inventions in performing its own obligations (§13.0, p0198) and being barred from using its own proprietary processes.

Why that clears the checklist:
- **Affiliates** — "IBM" is defined at §1.9 as IBM "and its Subsidiaries", so affiliate coverage is inherent; adding it would duplicate.
- **Contractors** — ownership permits IBM to extend rights freely, reinforced by §5.2(a)(ii) (transfer "to IBM or to another party that IBM designates").
- **Perpetual / irrevocable / no at-will revocation / successor transfer** — all inherent in title, so the position sits at or above preferred.

Other licence locations were checked and are not adverse: §13.3(a), the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement (§§5–6) and Attachment 6 all run **from IBM to MSL** and restrict the Vendor, so they are not flagged. The sentence in §24.1(a) that "MSL conveys to IBM no software title or license…" is a reciprocal no-implied-licence statement in the I/T system-access context, not a grant clause, and does not erode IBM's Product IP ownership.

Only cosmetic gap noted (not redlined): no express "contractors acting on IBM's behalf" phrase, immaterial given IBM owns the IP.
